```

  include: ["adapters/**/*.test.ts","packages/**/*.test.ts","tests/**/*.test.ts","tools/**/*.test.ts"]
  -> *.test.ts ONLY, so every .mjs misses; also no apps/**

```

So the file is not matched by the root vitest include (wrong extension), not in the `node --test` list, and not inside any package so no `--filter` reaches it. **No gate executes it.**

WHAT IT GUARDS, which is why this is filed HIGH rather than as a cleanup. It is task-bf2b2aac's DoD-4 end-to-end forgery harness: it stages a forged pnpm at PNPM_HOME and FIRST ON PATH, copies the repo to a temp directory, invokes the workflow's own pack-step script, and asserts BOTH that the ZIP is absent (or the step exited nonzero with the exact refusal code) AND that `FORGED_PNPM_EXECUTED` appears nowhere in stdout, stderr or the filesystem. Its only recorded executions are HAND-TYPED `node --test <path>` in that row's step-2 comment and its QA record. A supply-chain guard that no gate runs is indistinguishable from one that does, until it is not.

THE MECHANISM, worth keeping because it is not a typo: two files share a BASENAME one path segment apart — `tests/integration/release-supply-chain.test.mjs` and `tests/integration/release/release-supply-chain.test.mjs`. The script names one and the eye reads it as both. The discriminator is never the name; it is enumerating what the runner actually globs against what exists on disk.

RELATED FACT THE FIX MUST NOT BREAK: this repo has THREE disjoint test lanes, and a "repo-wide green" claim needs all three named. (1) `pnpm --filter <pkg> test` — package only, never sees `tests/**`. (2) root `pnpm test` — `tests/**/*.test.ts` etc, NEVER sees `apps/**` (already a global rail). (3) `pnpm test:integration` — adds the `node --test` .mjs half, which neither of the others can reach.

CONSUMER NOTE: no production bytes need to change. The likely shapes are a line in `test:integration`'s `node --test` list, or a rename/glob that the existing runner catches — the choice belongs in the plan, not here.
